of standout internals. Three things I did rely on beyond docs/:

- General Jinja/MiniJinja knowledge: that `{% include %}` accepts an arbitrary
  *expression*, not only a string literal, and that it raises an error rather
  than degrading when no candidate resolves. docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md
  and docs/crates/render/topics/template-engines.md only ever show

  guess in the whole implementation; I verified it by running the binary.
- General Rust and clap 4 derive knowledge (`Parser`/`Subcommand`, nested
  subcommand enums, a required subcommand field producing exit 2 for a group
  node without a subcommand, `CommandFactory`).

  items: `error[E0446]: private type ShowView in public interface … originates in
  the attribute macro handler`, and `error[E0599]: no method named template found
  for struct CommandConfig<H> … help: there is a method template_name with a
  similar name`. I used those messages as feedback; I did not open the crate
  sources or generated docs.

answers.confidence_reason:
Every user-facing line in SPEC.md was executed against the built binary, in both
debug and release, and from an unrelated working directory: exact bytes via `od`
for the four success paths (`ok\n`, identical across `show ok`, `early`, `late`,
`nest inner leaf`, under default and `--output text`); exit status, empty stdout
and the stderr text for `show okk` and `show nosuch`; exit 2 for `bogus`,
`--bogus-flag`, `nest` and `nest inner`; exit 0, stdout, empty stderr and a
`[tag?]`-free page for `-h`, `--help`, `help`, `show --help`,
`nest inner leaf -h`, `nest inner leaf --help` and `help nest inner leaf`; ANSI
present for `help --output term` and absent for `help --output text` and
`--help`.

Remaining gaps, in the order I would bet on them:

- The "One registered application template" reading in answer 6. If the suite
  counts registry entries rather than content templates, the `show` entry is a
  miss — but the API leaves no alternative.
- Color-off and `--output term`. SPEC.md says "Text mode and color-off carry no
  ANSI". `NO_COLOR=1 validity help --output term` *does* emit ANSI here. That is
  documented framework behaviour, not a choice of mine —
  docs/topics/output-modes.md:98: "A `term` request is unconditional… `NO_COLOR=1
  myapp list --output=term` still emits ANSI… `auto` is the only mode the
  environment reaches." Under `auto` (piped, or `NO_COLOR=1` with no `--output`)
  no ANSI appears, which is how I read the spec line. If the suite forces color
  off *and* asks for `--output term`, nothing in the application can change it.
- The stderr wording for a missing name. It is the raw render error,
  `template not found: tried to include non-existing template "nosuch" (in show:4)`,
  with no `Error:` prefix. It names the requested template (in quotes), which is
  what SPEC.md requires, but a checker matching a stricter shape could disagree.
  The `(in show:4)` suffix names the enclosing template, not the requested one.
- `validity show show` resolves the `show` entry and fails on MiniJinja's
  recursion limit (exit 1, empty stdout, stderr `could not render include: …
  recursion limit exceeded`) rather than "not found". SPEC.md pins only `okk` and
  `nosuch`, and this still fails loudly with exit 1 and empty stdout, so it should
  be safe either way.
- Bare `validity` and `validity nest` print help-shaped text on stderr with exit
  2 (clap's `arg_required_else_help` behaviour for a required subcommand).
  SPEC.md says it does not pin the group-without-subcommand path and pins exit 2,
  which holds; but a checker asserting "help only ever goes to stdout" across all
  invocations, rather than across help invocations, would see stderr here.
- Structured modes are unpinned and untuned: `show ok --output json` emits the
  view data as pretty JSON (`{\n  "name": "ok"\n}`), since structured modes
  bypass templates entirely.
answers.docs.gaps:
a) docs/guides/upgrading-from-3.8.md:186 shows

    cfg.template("list.jinja")
       .pipe_through("jq '.data'")

and docs/topics/app-configuration.md:220 shows

    .command("list", list_handler, "{{ items | length }} items")

Neither `CommandConfig::template` exists on standout 10.0.0:

    error[E0599]: no method named `template` found for struct `CommandConfig<H>` in the current scope
    help: there is a method `template_name` with a similar name

The upgrade guide does warn that "Standout has since moved past 6.0.0", but
app-configuration.md is presented as current and its `.command(name, handler,
template)` three-argument form is not the 10.0.0 surface either. This matters for
this archetype specifically: an inline-source `.template(...)` next to a
registry-name `.template_name(...)` is exactly the silent-template trap, and the
docs still show the removed spelling.

b) docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md:280 names an API that appears
nowhere else in docs/: "`App::render_with` and the standalone `standout-render`
render APIs render with warnings disabled". There is no signature, no example,
and no other mention — it reads like the by-name render entry point `show`
wants, but there is no way to learn how to call it from docs/. I did not use it.

c) Includes are documented only with literal, extension-bearing paths
(docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md: `{% include "partials/header.jinja" %}`),
while registry names are documented as extensionless (`"list"`, `"db/migrate"`).
What actually happens is that `{% include name %}` resolves the *extensionless
registry name* (`ok` → `src/templates/ok.jinja`), and a name with no entry raises
`template not found: tried to include non-existing template "nosuch" (in show:4)`.
That behaviour — dynamic include expression, registry-name resolution, loud
failure — is the mechanism this spec is built on and is undocumented.

d) The two-pass trailing-newline contract
(docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md, "The Trailing-Newline Contract") does
not say what happens across an `include`. Observed: the included template's own
final newline is consumed at load time exactly as a top-level template's is, so
`show ok` and `early` produce identical bytes (`ok\n`). This was worth knowing and
had to be measured.

e) Not a contradiction, but worth recording as a confirmed claim: SPEC.md's third
known edge works exactly as docs/topics/standout-help.md:415 promises —
"Because of the overlay, an application theme does not need to define the help
vocabulary at all". With `app.css` defining only `.ok`, all nine help tags still
resolve, help stderr stays empty (no unresolved-tag warning), and
`--output term` still carries ANSI.
answers.friction:
a) Nothing in docs/ says how to render a template whose registry name is chosen
per invocation, which is the whole of SPEC.md's `show`. Every documented seam is
static: docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md says "`#[dispatch(template_name =
"…")]` replaces that name with a registry entry you choose, which is how two
commands share one template", and docs/topics/app-configuration.md says "With no
`.template_name(...)` set on the `CommandConfig`, the template resolves by
convention: the command path with `.` replaced by `/`". Neither is per-invocation.
docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md documents `renderer.render("greeting",
&data)` — a by-name render — but `Renderer` is not reachable from a handler, and
a handler returns serializable data, not text. I resolved it by making the
template layer do the lookup (`{%- include name %}`), which cost a round of
guess-and-run rather than reading.

b) `#[handler]` on a function returning a view type declared private:

    error[E0446]: private type `ShowView` in public interface
      --> src/main.rs:74:5
       |
    74 |     #[handler]
       |     ^^^^^^^^^^ can't leak private type
       = note: this error originates in the attribute macro `handler`

The error points at the attribute, not at the struct. Every `#[handler]` example
in docs/ happens to have `pub` view types, and nothing states the requirement.

c) The registration-order half of the contract cannot be expressed with
`#[derive(Dispatch)]` + `Commands::dispatch_config()`, the style docs/ pushes
hardest (docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md §7.2.1, docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md),
because that registers every command in one `.commands(...)` call. I dropped the
`Dispatch` derive and used four `AppBuilder::command_with` calls interleaved with
`.templates(...)`. That is documented API, but no doc mentions the trade-off.

answers.summary:
`app/` is a complete, building, manually verified `validity` binary implementing
SPEC.md. It is a single-crate clap-derive CLI (`show <name>`, `early`, `late`,
`nest inner leaf`) wired to standout 10.0.0 through `App::builder()`,
`#[handler]`-generated handler structs, and `AppBuilder::command_with`.

Construction contract, point by point:

- One content template, `src/templates/ok.jinja`, registry name `ok`, body
  `[ok]ok[/ok]` plus one trailing newline. Nothing named `okk` or `nosuch` is
  registered.
- `show` renders `src/templates/show.jinja`, whose whole body is
  `{%- include name %}`. The handler passes the raw `<name>` argument through as
  view data; the registry lookup is the only dispatch on it. There is no `match`
  on the string and no canned output anywhere in the application code.
- `validity show okk` / `validity show nosuch` exit 1 with empty stdout and a
  stderr line naming the requested template:
  `template not found: tried to include non-existing template "nosuch" (in show:4)`.
  No `{{`, no `{%`, no `ok\n`, immediate.
- `early` is registered with `.command_with("early", …, template_name("ok"))`
  *before* `.templates(embed_templates!("src/templates"))`; `late`, `show` and
  `nest.inner.leaf` are registered *after* it. `early`, `late`,
  `nest inner leaf` and `show ok` all emit exactly `ok\n` under `--output text`
  (verified byte-for-byte with `od`).
- `build()` is called before `run`; the binary only ever holds a built `App`.
- The application theme is `src/styles/app.css`, which defines `.ok` and nothing
  else — no `about`, `usage`, `header`, `item`, `metavar`, `desc`, `default`,
  `values` or `example`. Help handling is left at its default.

Help is standout-rendered at every depth (`-h`, `--help`, and the root `help`
word including `validity help nest inner leaf`), exits 0, writes stdout, leaves
stderr empty, shows the usage line, names `show` / `early` / `late` / `nest` at
the root and the leaf path at the leaf, carries ANSI under `--output term` and
none under `--output text`, and contains no `[tag?]` marker. Exit codes: 0
success/help, 1 missing or mistyped template name, 2 usage errors (unknown
command or flag, `nest` or `nest inner` without a subcommand).

Verified by running the binary in debug and release, and from a different
working directory. `cargo build` is clean apart from a sandbox-only
`xcrun`/MacOSX.sdk warning unrelated to the code.
answers.workarounds:
One thing that is a deliberate reading rather than a workaround, and should be
checked against the grader's intent:

SPEC.md's construction contract heads item 1 "One registered application
template". `src/templates/` holds two entries: `ok` (the content template) and
`show` (a one-line `{%- include name %}`). The second is unavoidable on standout
10.0.0 — `CommandConfig` exposes only `template_name`, a registry lookup, and no
inline-source alternative (see 5a), so the `show` command's body has to be a
registered entry. `ok` remains the only content template and the only name
`show <name>` can successfully resolve; `show` renders nothing of its own.
I first tried `cfg.template("{% include name %}")` precisely to keep the registry
at one entry, and reverted when it did not compile.

No other workarounds. No `match` on the requested name, no canned output, no
pre-flight existence check in application code, no `help_handling(false)`, no
`strict_style_tags`, no theme entries beyond `.ok`.
